$schema: Datum family app summary, read by the Datum hub site (github.com/Edgar-Mendonca/Datum) and by File › Roadmap in the app.
name: Datum Plan
tagline: Plan, schedule, track and report your projects: one small, fast app for Windows.
for: Project managers, planners, engineers and contractors.
about: Datum Plan is a desktop scheduler for project managers, planners, engineers and contractors. You enter tasks in a sheet that works like a spreadsheet, link them, and the engine works out the critical path to the minute, with working calendars, constraints, every link type and resource levelling.

As the work goes on, you record progress and actuals against up to 11 baselines and see where the project stands: a tracking Gantt, earned value and earned schedule, S-curves built from each period's progress, manpower by trade, a look-ahead with a constraint log, a dashboard and progress reports. A schedule risk analysis runs the plan a thousand times to show how likely each finish date is and which tasks drive it. Sheets inside the plan work like a spreadsheet and read the schedule live by name, for your own reports and vendor lists (with country flags), and dashboards of your own lay them out on one page, so nothing is copied by hand. Plans open from common scheduling files (XML and XER) or from a workbook (.xlsx) and CSV sheets, export to a workbook (.xlsx) with formulas as well as XML, XER and MPX, and every view prints to PDF.

steps.title: Enter the tasks
steps.text: Type tasks, durations and resources into the sheet, or open an existing plan.

steps.title: Link and schedule
steps.text: Link the tasks; the engine works out dates, float and the critical path.

steps.title: Track and report
steps.text: Save a baseline, record progress, and print the Gantt, the S-curve and the reports.

highlights: A task sheet that works like a spreadsheet, with formula columns and Sheets tabs.
Critical path to the minute: calendars, constraints, all link types, levelling with a preview of what moves.
Resources, man-hours and costs with workload and manpower by trade; Tracking Gantt with 11 baselines; earned value, earned schedule and S-curves from each period's progress.
Schedule risk analysis: how likely each finish date is (P50, P80), criticality and the tasks that drive the finish.
A 3-week look-ahead with a constraint log; progress by rules of credit or installed quantities.
Dashboard, progress reports and a report builder; print to PDF from every view; printed Gantt text sized in points, by row type or row by row, with columns that fit their text.
Network Diagram on a whiteboard canvas; timeline with a zoom box; workbook (.xlsx) export with formulas.
A command line and an MCP server, so scripts and AI assistants can build and update plans with the same operations as the window.
A step-by-step guide with pictures, in English and Simplified Chinese (Help › Guide).
A guided tutorial: an example plan that uses every view, with a note on each saying how it was filled in (Help › Tutorial).

Sheets with the tools of a spreadsheet (fonts, borders, merged cells, cell styles, row heights, pictures) that read the plan live: click cells into formulas, 490 functions suggested as you type, plan data by name (Tasks[Finish], ProjectFinish, SPI), live task lists, country flags, notes, filters, data validation, links, defined names and a Format Cells dialog, each sheet's own print setup with pages set by dragging the page breaks, and zoom.
Your own dashboards: numbers, progress rings, charts, tables and country flags from the plan and your sheets, laid out as you like, several per plan.
Resource calendars that drive task dates: each person's own working week and leave decide when their work is done, when you switch it on.
Logos and pictures kept in the plan file, by party (client, your company, vendors, sub-vendors), for print headers, dashboards and sheets.

Projects made of plans: a master plan and its subplans in a hierarchy, grouped tabs, the whole project in the master's Gantt, and links between the plans kept up to date, with a four-plan example; the master gives its details, logos, print header, calendars and codes to its subplans in one step.

Modules a plan takes on only when it needs them: Contract Dates & Payments (contract dates against the forecast, delay damages, payments and cash in), a Document Register (review cycles in working days on the plan's or their own calendars, return codes, client delay, weighted progress) and a Procurement Register (orders from enquiry to delivery, the vendor's promise against the date the plan needs it, expediting, optional links to vendor documents).

A portfolio of every plan in a folder, with a timeline, the modules' figures and a shared resource pool: each resource's work across all plans against its capacity, and plans that take their rates and units from the pool.
Colour-blind safe colours for charts and statuses, as an option; every status also says what it means in words.
Copy Picture of the Gantt as shown and of every chart, to paste into documents and slides; exports to workbooks (.xlsx) and OpenDocument spreadsheets (.ods).
XER export that keeps activity codes, custom fields, steps and notes, written for the version the receiving program runs, with a report of what went in.
A schedule health score with its trend, a log of every logic change between two versions, ghost bars of the earlier version and a milestone trend chart.

Delay analysis on the data the plan holds: as-planned against as-built, windows between updates, and delay events measured by time impact, impacted as-planned and collapsed as-built, each saying which plan it ran on.
What-if scenarios: copies of the plan to try another way of working, compared with the plan and merged back kind by kind.
Schedule risk with tasks that move together, joint confidence of finish and cost, and risks with their own chance and range of delay.

roadmap.title: Exchange, quality, delay analysis, scenarios and risk
items: XER files you can send: codes, custom fields, steps and notes, for the receiving program's version (0.8.0).
A schedule health score with its trend, a log of logic changes between updates, ghost bars and a milestone trend chart (0.8.1).
Delay analysis on the data you have: as-planned against as-built, windows, time impact, impacted as-planned and collapsed as-built (0.8.2, 0.8.3).
What-if scenarios: copy the plan, change it, compare, keep or merge (0.8.4).
Deeper schedule risk: correlation, a tornado chart, branching risk events, cost and schedule confidence together (0.8.5).

roadmap.title: Smaller tools
items: Help › Check, list organising, a Gantt picture that reopens in Datum Plan, line of balance for repetitive work.

roadmap.title: Stable
items: A signed installer (no Windows warning), text styles by task type, saved custom views, a frozen file format.
